electric-violet.$description: Electric Violet — Primary brand accent — icon strokes, card borders, active link underlines, connection lines, and the dominant chromatic signal across product surfaces

bright-indigo.$description: Bright Indigo — Interactive links, active nav items, icon highlights, and secondary borders — a slightly lighter sibling to Electric Violet for hover/active states

deep-indigo.$description: Deep Indigo — Pressed/visited state of brand accent, dark text on light-violet surfaces, and the deepest chromatic token in the brand scale

soft-violet.$description: Soft Violet — Outlined button borders, light icon strokes, and lavender-toned hairlines — the pastel end of the brand ramp

lavender-mist.$description: Lavender Mist — Filled primary action background, soft chip/badge fills, and tinted section washes — the chromatic surface that makes CTAs feel warm without shouting

periwinkle-wash.$description: Periwinkle Wash — Soft tinted body backgrounds and gentle section highlights — used sparingly to break up white space

signal-green.$description: Signal Green — Green decorative accent for icons, marks, and small graphic details

paper.$description: Paper — Page canvas and card surface — the lightest layer, sits behind everything

fog.$description: Fog — Secondary surface, button hover fills, and section backgrounds — the step below Paper

cloud.$description: Cloud — Subtle button borders, inset surface fills, and the faintest hairline dividers

mist.$description: Mist — Card borders, subtle dividers, and disabled surfaces — the first gray that reads as a visible line

pale-steel.$description: Pale Steel — Icon fills and decorative shapes on light surfaces

silver.$description: Silver — Soft shadows, placeholder text in dark mode, and muted decorative fills

mid-gray.$description: Mid Gray — Muted icon fills, secondary button borders, and de-emphasized text

steel.$description: Steel — Caption text, nav meta, and medium-emphasis supporting copy

slate.$description: Slate — Body subtext, icon inactive state, and heading accents — the most-used muted text color

graphite.$description: Graphite — Body text on light tinted surfaces where pure black would feel too heavy

iron.$description: Iron — Primary text on light surfaces, most-used border color, and structural hairlines — the workhorse neutral

charcoal.$description: Charcoal — Secondary heading text and body emphasis

dark-steel.$description: Dark Steel — Heading text and strong body copy

onyx.$description: Onyx — Primary heading text, logo fill, and the darkest body text — near-black without the harshness of pure #000

near-black.$description: Near Black — Display headline text, primary button labels, and maximum-contrast text

marund.$description: Display and heading face — a humanist serif with personality. Used for hero headlines, section titles, and editorial moments. Tight tracking (-0.05em at 96px) pulls letters close for a confident, considered feel. Weights 400–450 for body, 500–600 for headlines. The custom stylistic sets 'ss00' and 'ss03' define its distinctive character.

inter-variable.$description: Body, UI, and secondary heading face — the operational typeface. Inter handles navigation, buttons, body copy, captions, labels, and supporting metadata. Weight 300 is used for light emphasis moments; 500–600 for button labels and nav links. The 0.14em tracking on small uppercase text creates the spaced-eyebrow label pattern seen above section headings.
